newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest direct hogs seen $0.50-$1 lower-dealers.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest direct hogs seen $0.50-$1 lower-dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices Monday were seen $0.50 to mostly $1.00 per cwt lower amid projections for slaughter cutbacks for the fifth consecutive week, livestock dealers said.
Packer operating margins were derailed by soft pork demand and industry overcapacity, they said. An increase in hog prices contributed to the weak margins, they said.

Slaughter picked up briefly earlier this week when pork prices drifted higher. The strength in product prices, however, was overwhelmed by increased hog values, which spurred packers to trim slaughter further, the dealers said.
Estimated Saturday hog slaughter was 20,000 head, compared with 26,000 last week and 12,000 last year, USDA reported.
The week to date figure of 1.622 million head was up 1.4 percent from last week's 1.599 million and down 4.1 from last year's 1.691 milion, USDA statistics showed.
Interior Iowa and southern Minnesota top prices for hogs delivered to the plant on Monday could range $60.00 to $60.50 and Illionis hogs could range $58.50 to $59.00 at plants.
Indiana-Ohio top hog prices at the plant were seen $59.00 to $59.50, the dealers said.
